name: InsideBar
quote: One simple way to quantify volatility contraction is by looking for inside bars, which are bars whose entire range is enclosed within the range of the previous bar.
description: The current bar's high is at or below the previous bar's high and its low is at or above the previous bar's low -- a single-bar volatility-contraction signal.

complexity.reason: a bare two-bar comparison of prices on fixed offsets

notes: Restates the corpus's existing InsideBar rule; recorded per the dedup-hint convention.

name: CloseNearBarExtremeShowsConviction
quote: a close near the high of the bar usually shows that buyers were in control going into the end of the time period. Conversely, closes near the middle of the bar... show a certain neutrality and lack of conviction.
description: The close sits in the upper fraction of the bar's own high-low range (long: buyer conviction); mirrored for a close near the low (seller conviction).

name: ConsecutiveClosesAtBarExtremeRun
quote: many more bars close at or near their high in a buying climax and on their low in a selling climax
description: For N consecutive bars, the close sits in the top fraction of each bar's own range (bull) -- a climax/exhaustion sign that also recurs in the chapter's 'character of trend legs' checklist.

name: LargeBarNearLegEndWarning
quote: very large bars near the end of a swing can indicate exhaustion or climax, which will usually be obvious on the lower time frame
description: A large-range bar (G03-04) occurring near the end of a trend leg (rather than early or mid-leg) is an exhaustion/climax warning, distinct from a large bar that just signals conviction.
pseudocode: (high[0]-low[0]) > rangeMultiple*average(high-low, rangeLookback) AND barsSince(legStart) >= legLength - nearEndBars

complexity.reason: reuses G03-04's window average; the leg-position test needs a defined leg start
